newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN EAGLE GROUP SAYS CHANGES ON BOARD.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN EAGLE GROUP SAYS CHANGES ON BOARD.

text.p: American Eagle Group Inc said Wednesday that four board members resigned their positions ahead of a previously scheduled July 31 streamlining of the insurance company's management structure.

The company said in a statement that Joseph Grant, Keith Hughes, James Maser and Elvis Mason have resigned as directors of the company. In addition, Frederick G. Anderson, senior vice president, general counsel and secretary has resigned effective July 31, 1997, and the position of general counsel will be eliminated.

American Eagle did say that Howard Putnam has been elected a director of the Company. Putnam is currently an author and consultant and previously worked as an airline executive at Braniff Interinational, Southwest Airlines and United Airlines.

The insurance company said the move was originally intended to take place after the completion of the sale of its aviation insurance business, the principal subsidiary of the Company, to the Great American Insurance Co.

Recently, the company said that Great American would not proceed with the acquisition of American Eagle's aviation insurance business under previously announced terms. The company said the Texas Department of Insurance has increased its regulatory oversight of the company by acting as conservator.

M. Philip Guthrie, chairman, president and chief executive officer of American Eagle Group told Reuters, "we entered into this conservation voluntarily, but aside from that I cannot comment further on the situation."

Previously, the department informed the aviation unit it has reached an agreement in principle with Great American under which Great American will continue to write new and renewal aviation business. Wednesday, 23 July 1997 20:09:02 ENDS nN23225691
